title: Vertical Sleeve Gastrectomy Protocol
author: Kristin Evans
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.za3f2gn

steps.title: Pre-operative Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the animals and the surgical environment.

substeps.instruction: Fast animals overnight to empty stomach and intestines.
Weight animals to calculate Meloxicam and Baytril dosing.
Autoclave all supplies and tools; start the bead sterilizer for instruments.
Prepare a sterile field around the microscope and surgisuite surgical platform and turn on the warming field.
Place sterilized supplies onto the sterile field.

steps.title: Anesthesia and Site Preparation
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal and prepare the surgical site.

substeps.instruction: Induce anesthesia using isoflurane chamber at 5% to effect, then maintain at 1-1.5% isoflurane in the prep area.
Apply artificial tear salve to each cornea.
Clip hair from the ventrum from the knee to the armpit area.

Perform a surgical scrub: initial wipe of Betadine followed by 70% alcohol (working outward from the incision line), then three successive scrubs of Betadine followed by 70% alcohol using clean cotton-tipped applicators for each application.
Administer Meloxicam SR 2 mg/kg subcutaneously in the rear dorsal area.
Spray the incision area with betadine solution before transferring the animal to the surgical area.

steps.title: Surgeon Sterilization
steps.instruction: The surgeon must wash and dry hands with soap and water and don sterile surgical gloves.

steps.title: Stomach Isolation
steps.instruction: Expose and isolate the stomach from surrounding tissues.

substeps.instruction: Make a small vertical midline skin incision from just below the xiphoid process to the mid abdomen at the height of the top of the hip.
Cut along the linea alba from the xiphoid to just below the umbilical region.
Pull the intestine away using gloved fingers or a sterile cotton tip applicator to expose the stomach.
Elevate the stomach through the incision by placing a dry sterile cotton tip applicator under the median and left liver lobes and under the stomach.
Bluntly dissect ligamentous fat from the stomach using a sterile cotton tip applicator and tuck it back into the abdomen.
Remove the ligament to the liver in the lesser curvature of the stomach using small iris scissors.
Remove the ligament connecting the fundus to the body wall using small iris scissors.
Elevate the vascular gastrosplenic ligament connection using a cotton tip applicator.
Fuse the vascular connection using electrocautery to free the stomach.

steps.title: Vertical Sleeve Gastrectomy
steps.instruction: Perform the gastric resection to remove 75-80% of the stomach.

substeps.instruction: Moisten the stomach and intestine with sterile saline using a gavage needle, avoiding pulling the stomach out of the body cavity (to protect vagus nerves) and avoiding manipulation of the pancreas attachment at the pyloric portion.
Place the isolated stomach on a 2 x 2 gauze and irrigate with sterile saline.
Make an incision using micro-scissors along the avascular seam of the greater curvature from the right of the esophagus to the pancreatic vessel attachment.
Gently remove stomach contents onto the gauze using a cotton tip applicator.
Flush the stomach area with sterile saline and replace the gauze with a fresh wet piece.
Size the gastric pouch remnant from the esophagus to the pylorus using sterile 7 French Polyethylene tubing.

Close the stomach at the edge of the sizing (using 6 French tubing) with 7-0 PDS suture using a simple continuous suture through both stomach wall layers, creating a diagonal line from the right of the esophagus to the pancreatic connecting vessels (leaving ~1/3 of the stomach cranial to the suture line).
Keep the remaining length of suture attached.
Cut away the stomach tissue distal to the suture line using micro scissors, ensuring the suture material is not cut.
Close the stomach using 7-0 PDS in a continuous mattress pattern from the pancreatic vessels to the esophagus.
Apply additional single interrupted sutures to any noted gap areas.
Verify the remaining pouch has a lumen diameter sized to 6 French and approximates 20-25% of the original stomach area.

steps.title: SHAM Vertical Sleeve Gastrectomy
steps.instruction: Perform the sham procedure if applicable.

substeps.instruction: Apply gentle pressure to the stomach using hemostats approximately 2/3 cranial to the greater curvature (gauge location using 6 French tubing externally from esophagus to pylorus).
Run two separate pieces of 7-0 suture through the outer layer of the stomach wall on both sides, just below the pressure line.

steps.title: Surgical Closure
steps.instruction: Clean the abdominal cavity and close the incisions.

substeps.instruction: Perform abdominal lavage with at least 25 ml of sterile saline using a gavage needle for 4 gavages (total 100 ml).
Change the gauze under the stomach before the lavage and with each successive lavage.
Place the stomach back into the abdomen.
Suction remaining saline using sterile cotton tip applicators and gauze.
Instill Baytril (20 mg/kg) diluted in sterile saline into the abdominal cavity.
Close the linea alba abdominal wall with 6-0 PDS in a simple continuous pattern.
Close the skin with 6-0 PDS in a simple continuous pattern.
Apply tissue glue over the suture line.

steps.title: Post-operative Care
steps.instruction: Provide recovery support and monitor animal health.

substeps.instruction: Provide a slurry diet (powdered original or test diet combined with water in a 1:1 ratio) for 3 days, replaced daily.
Administer 1 ml subcutaneous saline for the first three days.
Transition animals to regular chow pellets at Day 3 post-surgery; implement pair feeding between CSG and pair fed Sham controls.
Observe animals once to twice daily for the first 3 days, then daily for the next 10 days (14 days total), assessing pain, incision, eating, fecal production, and hydration.
Collect body weights: prior to surgery, on the day of surgery, at 3 days, 10 days, and 14 days post-operative.
